problem: The chapter says to address line 1 from 0x00 and line 2 from 0x40, then says 'send the address as a command'. A student will send 0x00 or 0x40 as the command byte. The set-DDRAM-address command needs bit 7 set, so plain 0x40 is a different command (set CGRAM address).
fix: Say the command byte is 0x80 + address: line 1 starts at 0x80, line 2 at 0xC0. The 0x00 and 0x40 are the addresses inside the command.

problem: The busy flag rule is given only for the 8-bit bus. In 4-bit mode D7 is not on the first nibble read; the program must read the high nibble (which carries BF) and then a second nibble to finish the read. A student in 4-bit mode will poll wrongly.
fix: Add: in 4-bit mode, read the high nibble first (BF is bit D7 of that nibble), then read the low nibble to complete the byte, before checking BF.

problem: Two of the three listed cures do not stop ghosting. 'Scan one key at a time' does not help: the ghost path runs through the two pressed keys of the L, whatever the row drive is. Only series diodes, or rejecting a row where more than one column reads 0, remove the ghost.
fix: Use diodes in series with each key, or accept a key only when exactly one column reads 0 in that row (reject multi-column rows). Drop 'scan one key at a time'.

problem: The note 'A 300 Ω resistor is not a common E12 value' is true but misleading: 300 Ω is a standard E24 value and is sold. Calling 330 Ω 'the nearest listed standard value' implies 300 Ω does not exist.
fix: Say: 300 Ω is an E24 value; in the coarse E12 series the neighbours are 270 Ω and 330 Ω, and 330 Ω is picked because it keeps the current below the wanted 10 mA (about 9.1 mA).
